title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and adaptive timeouts
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Continuous batching improved throughput but we observed request unfairness under skewed size distributions and occasional starvation of low-priority short requests during high-volume loads. This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to reduce queueing unfairness, add starvation prevention mechanisms, and introduce adaptive timeouts so latency-sensitive requests get bounded wait times. Changes: - Introduce per-queue aging and dynamic priority decay to prevent indefinite starvation: requests gain priority based on wall-clock wait and token-size-normalized wait. - Implement max_wait and preemption thresholds: a request that exceeds max_wait is scheduled ahead of some batched candidates to bound tail latency. max_wait is configurable per route and defaults to 50ms for interactive routes. - Add an adaptive batch-assembly timeout that short-circuits batching when estimated remaining batch benefit is low (based on current queue composition and per-request token budget). - Update the batching heuristic to consider both request token cost and KV-cache reuse probability to improve kernel utilization without penalizing short requests. - Add new telemetry: queue_wait_histogram, preempt_count, starvation_rescue_count, adaptive_timeout_triggered. - Add unit and integration tests that simulate heavy skew, high-concurrency interactive traffic, and KV-cache hit/miss patterns. - Update config proto, docs, and a perf microbenchmark harness to reproduce previously observed regression and show improvement. Backwards compatibility: All behavior is opt-in via the continuous-batcher config flags; default rollout follows a conservative profile that preserves previous behavior unless routes opt into fairness/timeouts. Testing & results: Microbenchmark against the continuous-batcher benchmark harness shows 95th percentile latency for short requests reduced by ~35% under a heavy skewed load (90% large requests, 10% short interactive requests) at comparable throughput. No regressions on steady-state throughput observed on our Dedicated CI GPU fleet. Checklist: - [x] Scheduler algorithm implemented and covered by unit tests. - [x] Integration tests for starvation scenarios. - [x] Perf harness and benchmark results attached. - [x] Documentation and config comments added. - [x] Feature gated and defaulted conservatively for gradual rollout. Related: ENG-3241 (scheduler fairness), ENG-3298 (interactive latency SLOs).

discussion: Evan Miller (reviewer): Overall looks good. Two requests: (1) can we make the default max_wait per-route configurable via route-level metadata? (2) add more explanation in docs about how priority aging interacts with KV-cache reuse.

Aisha Patel (author): Addressed (1) — added route-level max_wait override and clarified defaults in config.proto and docs. For (2) expanded heuristics.md to add a short worked example showing how KV-cache probability modifies effective cost.

Priya Shah (reviewer): CI flaky on test_scheduler_starvation in the first run — looks like a timing assertion too tight on slower CI boxes. Can we make the test use retry/polling instead of fixed sleeps?

Aisha Patel (author): Fixed tests to use polling and extended thresholds. Re-ran CI; initial flaky test passed on rerun. Also added a short note in test harness about expected noise on slower machines.

Tomás Alvarez (approver): Benchmarks look convincing. Approve pending small nits: rename variable 'age_score' -> 'wait_score' and add a comment on preemption costs. I applied those nits in the last commit.

CI: First run: build passed, unit tests had 1 flaky failure (test_scheduler_starvation) — rerun completed successfully. Perf runs executed on the Dedicated CI fleet and attached artifacts are in the PR comment thread.
Merge: Squash merge chosen to keep history concise. Rollout: gated feature; ops to enable for /interactive routes in next canary window.
release_notes: Improved continuous-batcher scheduling: reduced tail latency for short requests under skewed loads via priority aging, max_wait preemption, and adaptive batching timeouts. Feature gated; see docs/perf/continuous-batcher.md for tuning guidance.
perf_summary: 95th percentile latency for short requests reduced by ~35% under skewed mixed-size workloads at similar throughput; no throughput regressions observed in Dedicated CI.
notes: Feature is gated behind continuous-batcher.fairness.enabled and continuous-batcher.timeouts.max_wait route-level config. Ops and SRE notified for gradual rollout to canary clusters.
